title: The Last Bowl
text:
Uncle Lim has stirred the same pot of soup for forty-one years. He arrives at four in the morning, when the hawker centre is dark and the metal shutters are still down, and he does not stop until the last bowl is sold.
His customers have grown up in front of him. The schoolboy who once needed a booster seat now brings his own daughter, and orders exactly what he ordered thirty years ago: extra noodles, less chilli.
Next month, the stall will close. Uncle Lim's hands are not what they were, and his children have chosen other work. He says he is not sad, only grateful. "A recipe is easy to write down," he tells anyone who asks. "What is hard is standing here every single morning, for somebody else's breakfast."
